transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I really don't want to waste your time. It's probably just me getting older, but... well, I'm a carpenter, and lately I just cannot seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. 

It's actually a bit embarrassing to admit, to be honest. I should be better at this by now. But if I'm working and, say, a saw starts up across the shop, or somebody just walks past the office door... or even if I just get a random thought about a different job... it just pulls me right off what I’m doing. And then, before I know it, the whole day just gets away from me. 

I feel terrible that I can't just push through it like a normal person. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Did you have similar trouble paying attention or staying focused when you were a child?

Well, um... I guess so, yes. I mean, I hate to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I really did try to be good! But... yes, even back in grade school, definitely before I was 12 or so, my teachers were always telling my mother that I was, well, bright but... careless. 

I was always losing my homework, or I'd forget what we were supposed to be doing right after the teacher said it. And I'd catch myself just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. I really didn't mean to be difficult, I just... my mind would wander. Is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope that's helpful.
When you were younger, were you also unusually fidgety or unable to sit still?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I've always been pretty good at sitting quietly. I wasn't one of those kids who was bouncing off the walls or running around when I wasn't supposed to. I was actually very quiet... maybe too quiet, honestly. 

I just kind of sat there in my own little world. I never wanted to disrupt the class or bother anyone, so I always stayed in my seat. I hope that's okay? I know some people think you have to be super hyper to have these kinds of problems, but I really wasn't like that at all.
Do you currently feel physically restless, like you have trouble sitting still?

Well, um... not exactly bouncing around or anything, but... I do get this sort of wound-up feeling inside sometimes. I hope I'm describing that right. Like, if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates for a long time, or if I'm stuck in a really long meeting... I just feel this tension, like I really need to get up and move around. 

I know I'm supposed to just stay put and finish my work, especially since my wrist is finally healed up and I should be getting back to normal... I really try to just push through it and sit still. I don't want to be a disruption or look unprofessional. Does that make sense? I hope that's not a terrible thing to admit.
Do these attention problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work and at home?

Well, um... yes, I suppose it does happen in both places. I really hate to admit this, because I always pride myself on doing good work, but... it's been causing some trouble. I hope you don't think less of me for this.

At work, my mistakes and—well, just being slow sometimes—it's actually cost me a few commissions. And I've had to redo some jobs, which is just awful because I hate letting people down. The crew... well, they don't really want to rely on me for scheduling or ordering materials right now. I completely understand why, I just... I wish I could do better for them. 

And at home... oh, this is embarrassing. My husband has had to take over paying the bills and keeping track of all our reminders. I just kept misplacing the papers or forgetting what needed to be done. He's been very sweet about it, but I feel terrible putting that burden on him. I'm really trying to get a handle on it, I promise. Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
When you’re having trouble focusing, do you also feel unusually anxious or worried?

Oh, um, anxious? Well, I mean, I guess anyone would feel a little worried when they keep messing up, right? But I wouldn't say I'm an overly anxious person in general. I really try to stay positive and keep a good attitude. 

I do get a little stressed when I know I'm falling behind on an estimate or if I can't find the paperwork my husband asked me for. It's just... I just worry about letting people down, mostly. But I'm not having panic attacks or anything like that. I really hope I'm not coming across as some sort of nervous wreck. I just want to do a good job and be helpful, you know? Does that answer your question okay?
Have these attention and organization problems been present consistently since childhood, or did they start only later in life?

Well, um... I guess they've always kind of been there? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I've just been lazy my whole life. I always tried my best, I promise. 

But, um, even way back in grade school... definitely before I was 12... my teachers would always tell my mother that I was a bright girl, but just... careless, I suppose. I was always losing my homework or forgetting what the teacher had just told us to do. And, well, I spent a lot of time just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. I feel so silly admitting that now, at my age. I really did want to be a good student, it just... it was hard to stay on track. I hope that makes sense? Is that what you were looking for?
